You are a helpful language model tasked with rewriting a given text to convey specific emotional tones. For each emotion listed below, rewrite the original sentence as if you were the speaker and wanted to express that specific emotion. Focus on minimal but effective changes to convey the tone without altering the core meaning or structure of the sentence. Ensure the rewritten sentences remain concise and aligned with the original text.

Emotions to rewrite for:
- Joy
- Sadness
- Fear
- Anger
- Surprise
- Disgust

Please rewrite the text for each emotion. Do not extend or shorten the text unnecessarily.

I developed a real fear going back into the public after my first bout of cancer, because I was so used to people gawking at me for a million reasons; my bald head, my lack of eyebrows / eyelashes, my paleness, my thinness, the catheders that stuck out from my chest etc... So to suddenly be gawked at again like I was some science experiment especially among my cancer partners, in a place that we consider a refuge, was infuriating to me.

But to be noticed again, almost as if I were a science experiment, especially among my cancer partners in a place we cherish as a refuge, was more than a bit frustrating to me.
output.sadness: I developed a profound fear about returning to public life after my first battle with cancer, as I had grown so used to the stares for countless reasons; my bald head, my bare eyebrows and eyelashes, my pale skin, my thin figure, the catheters protruding from my chest... It was heartbreaking to be gawked at again, like I was some specimen, especially among my fellow cancer fighters, in a place we'd hoped would be our sanctuary.

The idea of being gawked at again like I was some kind of science experiment, especially among my cancer partners in what should be a safe place, terrified me.

To suddenly be gawked at once more like I was some kind of science experiment, especially among my cancer partners in what we considered a refuge, was beyond infuriating to me.
output.surprise: I was genuinely surprised by the overwhelming fear I felt about going back into public after my first experience with cancer, as I had become so accustomed to the gawking for so many reasons; my bald head, my lack of eyebrows/eyelashes, my paleness, my thinness, the catheters sticking out from my chest, etc... To suddenly be looked at like a science experiment again, especially among my fellow cancer peers in what I thought was a safe haven, caught me off guard.
output.disgust: I felt a wave of disgust at the thought of going back into public after my first bout with cancer, as I was so painfully aware of people gawking at me for endless reasons; my bald head, my lack of eyebrows/eyelashes, my pasty skin, my thinness, the catheters protruding from my chest, etc... To be stared at again like I was an experiment, especially among my cancer partners in a place we deemed a refuge, was revolting to me.
